newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed higher on technical buying. May added $4.60 to close at $312.30 per tonne, while August was up $4.20 to close at $312.0 per tonne. Attention was focused on the New York March contract which broke through 11 cents/lb and touched off buy stops.

Other factors responsible for the upward move were a dearth of selling in the March contract and talk that tax-free sugar exports in Brazil are still under study. However, another good crop is forthcoming in Brazil.

Even if the weather had been unfavorable higher productivity would have guaranteed that the 1997/98 crop would be at least the same as last year. However, weather has been very beneficial and conditions are near to ideal, which points to another large crop in the 1997/98 season. It is estimated that at least five per cent more cane will be available for crushing in the Center/South region in 1997/98 which means that there will be an additional 10 to 15 million tonnes of cane, or perhaps even more.

Heavy rains in late 1996 meant that the 1996/97 campaign had to be cut short in several areas. The result was that about 4 million tonnes of cane were left standing and will be available to allow harvesting to start early this season. This should give the optimists food for thought and puts the rise in prices into perspective. March added 33 points to close at 11.25 cents/lb, while May ended 27 points higher at 11.15 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 11 and 18 points.
FUNDAMENTALS - SOUTH AFRICA - Sugar exports in

May/December 1996 reached 848,944 tonnes, raw value, up from 371,693 tonnes exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in crop year 1995/96 reached 380,200 tonnes, up from 354,820 tonnes the previous year. The rise in exports is the result of a recovery in production after a long period of drought. Main markets for South African raw sugar are Japan and South Korea, while white sugar is mainly exported to Israel, Saudi Arabia and African countries.

SWAZILAND - Sugar production in Swaziland in May/November 1996 reached 445,373 tonnes, raw value, up from 408,351 tonnes produced the same period in 1995. Total production in crop year 1995/96 (May/April) reached 413,945 tonnes, down from 478,833 tonnes produced the previous year.
TENDERS - The European Union awarded 17,000 tonnes of

white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 44.008 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on Wednesday. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to February 19 reached 1,532,850 tonnes, which compares to 1,598,948 tonnes last year. Mauritius is holding a buying tender for one cargo of white sugar for shipment between March to June. No further details were immediately available.
